Theorem
[Strong maximum principle for scalar equations] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0208 1. ch12:12.40\group Strong Scalar Maximum Principles

Assume $c\leq 0$. If $u\in C^{2,1}(D)\cap C^0(D\cup \gamma (D))$ satisfies $Lu\geq 0$ and attains a nonnegative maximum at $(x_0,t_0)\in D\cup \gamma (D)$, then \[ u(x,t)=u(x_0,t_0)qquad ((x,t)\in \overline{S(x_0,t_0)}). \]

Proof

\sketch ↗ thm:euclidean-parabolic-strong-maximum-principle Choose coordinate cylinders along any admissible curve to $(x_0,t_0)$. Theorem 4.1 makes the maximum set backward-open in each cylinder; continuity makes it closed. The connected chain of cylinders therefore lies in the maximum set. Taking closures proves the assertion.

□
